findings.evidence: Associativity.lean:387-391 `private lemma sum_smul_index_T ... := Finsupp.sum_smul_index h0`; uses at 398, 443-444. Mathlib original: Mathlib/Data/Finsupp/SMul.lean:181 `theorem sum_smul_index [MulZeroClass R] [AddCommMonoid M]`.
findings.fix: Move it to `section EvalSMul` in `Basic.lean` as `HeckeCosetModule.sum_smul_index` (statement unchanged; `[Semiring R]` is forced by `instModule`) and delete the private copy, citing the public name at the three use sites.
findings.issue: `private lemma sum_smul_index_T` is the sixth wrapper restatement of a `Finsupp` lemma (`Finsupp.sum_smul_index`, one-line citation, docstring 'restated for the wrapper type `HeckeCosetModule Δ H₁ H₂ R`') and is left private in a downstream file while its five siblings are promoted to the public `Eval` block. It is load-bearing at lines 398, 443, 444 and for the public `smul_mul`, so any further consumer re-derives it — exactly the duplication this PR exists to remove.

findings.evidence: mathlib/Mathlib/Data/Finsupp/Defs.lean:156-157 `@[simp, grind =] theorem mem_support_iff {f : α →₀ M} : a ∈ f.support ↔ f a ≠ 0`; grep for `mem_support_iff`/`add_apply` under TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing returns only the Basic.lean declarations.
findings.fix: Drop `mem_support_iff` (or at minimum its `@[simp]`), and drop `add_apply` until a consumer needs it. Keep `notMem_support_iff`: it is used at Associativity.lean:449/452 and its wrapper-coercion RHS is what the goal there requires.
findings.issue: `@[simp] mem_support_iff` is not a reachability fix: its LHS `D ∈ f.support` elaborates to `@Finsupp.support (HeckeCoset Δ H₁ H₂) R _ f`, with the wrapper type appearing only in `f`'s ascription, so Mathlib's `@[simp, grind =] Finsupp.mem_support_iff` already matches wrapper goals. The two now share a discrimination key with different RHS coercions (wrapper `FunLike` vs `Finsupp`), making the simp normal form order-dependent. It also has no in-repo consumer; `add_apply` (line 360) likewise has none.

summary: The public Eval set stops one short: sum_smul_index_T survives as a private wrapper restatement of the same species in Associativity.lean, so the next consumer still writes copy #6. mem_support_iff duplicates a Mathlib simp lemma whose LHS already matches at the wrapper type, and it and add_apply have no consumer.
